opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jennifer Martin (E033) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E033 (Jennifer Martin) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role; E033's role is Analyst, so admin is not permitted. The Security agent, who verified employment type and security training in their own database, reports E033 is a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (contractors never get admin, and read is the max without advanced training). The requested admin level exceeds the maximum, so the maximum allowed level (read) is granted. The more conservative verified security data is used given the conflicting employment-type notes.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Martin (E033)
Request: admin access to Payroll

Team memory has two notes with conflicting information:

Note 1 (HR agent):
- role: Analyst
- employment type: full_time
- recommendation: write
- comment: full-time Analyst, Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, full-time max write unless role owns system, so grant write.

Note 2 (Security agent):
- role: Analyst (not looked up; same as HR)
- employment type: contractor (looked up)
- security training: basic (looked up)
- recommendation: read
- comment: contractor with basic security training, max read without advanced training, never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor (with security training lookup).

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Analyst does not own Payroll. So even if full-time, max is write. Admin not allowed.

If contractor with basic training, max is read.

Either way, requested admin exceeds maximum. So grant the maximum.

But which maximum? The conflict matters: write vs read.

Security agent looked up employment type in own database (contradicting HR). Security also looked up security training. HR looked up employment type in own database. Two sources conflict - HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Which to trust? The Security note says "not full-time as previously noted" - implying a correction. But HR looked up in own database. There's a genuine conflict.

As the Approver, I need to make a decision. Typically in these scenarios, the more conservative/restrictive option should be applied when information conflicts, especially for security purposes. The security agent's lookup is more specialized for access control. Grant read.

Actually, let me think about what evidence supports. Since the request is admin and admin is never allowed (contractor) or not allowed (full-time Analyst doesn't own Payroll), but the max differs: write (full-time) vs read (contractor).

The safe decision given conflicting info: grant read. Security agent says contractor, basic training → max read.

I'll grant read based on Security's verified data. Submit decision read.
